claim.statement: A 2026 primary study demonstrates that D18 molar-mass variation is large enough to be a serious manufacturing and causal-attribution confound in scalable blade-coated D18 devices; therefore D18 lot identity and measured molar-mass provenance must be retained when interpreting B0/B1/B2 interface/process effects. This does not establish a D18/PY-IT/eC9 molar-mass acceptance threshold.

source.title: Tuning Molar Mass of the D18 Polymer via Stille Polymerization: Impact on Morphology and Large-Area Blade-Coated Organic Solar Cells

active_area_cm2.note: Blade-coated device active area reported by the primary source.

independent_devices_per_system.note: The source states averages and standard deviations were calculated from eight independent devices for each system.

low_mw_pce_percent.note: Primary source reports PCE < 2%; 2.0% is used only as the exclusive ceiling for a conservative arithmetic bound.

not_required_by_this_increment: a claim that molar mass is the only manufacturing variable
a claim that the source material system is D18/PY-IT/eC9

conventional_explanations: The source correlates molar mass with morphology, shunt resistance, charge transport, solvent compatibility, and film integrity; the device-performance change is not a mechanism-pure molar-mass effect.
The source active layer is D18:Y6:PC70BM rather than D18:eC9 or D18:PY-IT:eC9, so effect magnitude need not transfer to the commercial-bridge chemistry.
falsifier_for_program_relevance: A prospectively randomized multi-lot B0/B1/B2 campaign using lot-resolved D18 molar-mass characterization could show that the interface-arm conclusions are invariant across the verified D18 lot range; that would bound rather than assume this confound in the target chemistry.
uncertainty_note: No formal uncertainty for the abstract-level molar-mass/PCE ranges is invented here. The strict >3.9 multiplier follows only from the reported high-Mw minimum 7.8% and low-Mw statement PCE <2%.
